setup: Back on the pad, forearms on the arm rests
Grip the handles; let your legs hang
Press your shoulders down, away from your ears
execution: Lift your knees up toward your chest
At the top, tilt your hips up off the back pad
Pause, then lower your legs slowly
Stop the legs before they swing
faults: Don't stop at hip height without the hip tilt

notes: Climb on and off using the side steps; don't jump down.
Lower each rep under control so the legs don't swing into the next.
If your shoulders or elbows are uncomfortable on the pads, the reverse crunch trains the same curl lying down.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Reverse crunch
regressions.reason: Same pelvic curl lying on the floor; easier.

progressions.name: Captain's chair straight-leg raise
progressions.reason: Straight legs make a longer lever; much harder.

progressions.name: Hanging knee raise
progressions.reason: No back pad, so more grip and control are needed.

substitutions.name: Hanging knee raise
substitutions.reason: Same knee raise from a pull-up bar.

substitutions.name: Lying leg raise
substitutions.reason: Hip lift on the floor when the station is busy.

substitutions.name: Ab crunch machine
substitutions.reason: Stack-loaded ab work; curls from the ribs instead.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at hip height of a figure in a captain's chair (vertical back pad, forearm rests with handles). Feet hang clear of the floor.

keyPositions.label: Hang
keyPositions.describe: Back against the pad, forearms on the rests, hands on the handles, shoulders pressed down. Legs hang straight down with the knees soft.

keyPositions.label: Knees up
keyPositions.describe: Knees raised above hip height toward the chest, knees bent. Pelvis tilted up so the lower back eases off the pad. Shoulders still down.

ikHints: Forearms fixed on the rests and upper back on the pad in every frame
emphasise: Knees lift and the pelvis tilts up at the top

sources.title: ACE press release (2001): ACE-sponsored study reveals best and worst abdominal exercises
sources.supports: primaryMuscles and secondaryMuscles (captain's chair ranked in the top three for rectus abdominis and first for obliques by EMG, 30 adults)
sources.note: Press release, not a peer-reviewed paper. Muscle activity is not the same as growth.

uncertain.note: StrengthLog lists the hip flexors as a primary muscle; they are listed as primary with the abs (vocabulary word added 23 Oct 2026, expansion research Q1). The abs come first because the cues ask for the pelvis to curl.

UK gyms often call this station a "Roman chair", but "Roman chair back extension" is an alias of the 45° back extension (expansion research Q6). Only the specific "Roman chair knee raise" is an alias here. Plain "Knee raise" stays with Hanging knee raise. "Captain's chair" alone names the station; most people log it for this exercise, but Ben should confirm.
There is no captain's-chair station value. dip_station is the nearest, because the chair is usually part of a dip tower.
Approximate drawing targets, not measured data.
